finding: Patent claiming blood gene-expression markers (defensin alpha1, haemoglobin, CXCR4, tubulin beta 1, STK17B, HLA-DR, PTGDS) as CFS/ME diagnostic markers; abstract gives no data.
Narrative review claiming acupuncture at Siguan points helps CFS.
Diurnal urinary free cortisol and cortisone were lower across the day in CFS, while cortisol metabolites did not differ; supports reduced basal HPA function.
note: Sample size not in abstract; medication/psychiatric comorbidity excluded

finding: Interviews of young people and parents about a community rehabilitation programme reported perceived improvement and valued the approach.
Brewers' yeast extract raised running activity and lowered splenic IFN-gamma and IL-10 mRNA in a mouse CFS model.
Resting muscle free Mg2+ was higher in CFS (0.47 vs 0.36 mM, p<0.01) while PCr recovery after exercise did not differ.
note: Reanalysis of earlier data; no PCr recovery difference, unlike Newcastle studies

finding: Only CFS patients with high mental-fatigue scores showed impaired spatial working memory and sustained attention, with decline late in the test (cognitive fatigability).
GP-based survey: 73% girls, median illness 3.3 years; diagnosis made in 55%, mostly moderate severity.
PhD thesis on masculinity and health with one ME focus group.
Post-exertional malaise, unrefreshing sleep and impaired memory best discriminated CFS from MDD and controls (84-91% classified).
Goal attainment predicted quality-of-life improvement in a supportive group programme.
Generalised joint hypermobility was more frequent in CFS (20.6% vs 4.3%); no link with musculoskeletal pain.

population: Chronic fatigue in neurological disease (MS, encephalopathy)
finding: Fezam reduced fatigue in patients with brain damage; not ME/CFS.
At mean 3-year follow-up most regarded themselves recovered but about one third still had disabling symptoms; school absence high.
Six-month CBT and graded exercise programme improved HRQoL/psychosocial scores; exercise capacity changed modestly and barely correlated with them.
Patent for rhodiola, astragalus and angelica herbal composition.
Patent for transdermal androgen gel for CFS and fibromyalgia.
Empirical classification of CFS differed little from surveillance criteria; empirical CFS had worse impairment and fatigue.
Only half of surveyed GPs believed CFS exists; knowledge in primary care low.
Serum zinc was lower in CFS, correlating with severity, inflammation markers and reduced T-cell CD69 activation.
Intracellular perforin was reduced in NK cells (and indicatively in cytotoxic T cells) in CFS, a possible basis for reduced NK cytotoxicity.
Children with CFS had more somatic symptoms, more biological precipitants and infections, and less premorbid psychiatric history than emotional-disorder controls, with notable comorbidity.
Orthostatic instability on tilt was no more frequent in CFS (30%) than controls (48%); all CFS cases were POTS.
note: Population-based, tilt results may reflect hydration

finding: Mental and physical fatigue showed unreliable week-to-week variability; other physiological and cognitive measures were stable.
Support-group members valued legitimisation and information; active members reported greater symptom severity.
Women attributed CFS to a mix of viral triggers, stress and lifestyle.
Employment status correlated weakly with SF-36 subscales and peak workload.
Omega-6 fatty acids were higher and omega-3/omega-6 ratio lower in CFS, correlating with severity, low zinc and T-cell activation defects.
Previously reported urinary amino/organic acid markers (CFSUM1/2) were not confirmed; some evidence of inflammation and reduced intramuscular collagen.
Memory quotient lower in CFS (85 vs 98) with high rates of memory/attention complaints.

population: Mixed chronic disease (ME one of several)
finding: Self-management course gains were sustained at 12 months in a mixed chronic-disease group.
Reanalysis: CFS patients could not sustain a walking programme beyond 4-10 days, with worsening symptoms, suggesting exercise intolerance.
Narrative analysis of illness experience (restitution, chaos, quest).
Plasma and urinary free and acyl carnitine did not differ between CFS and controls.
Elastase activity was the sole predictor of reduced VO2 at RER 1.0; RNase L measures also examined, linking intracellular immune dysregulation to exercise performance.
After a maximal exercise test CFS fatigue stayed raised for up to 2 days while controls recovered within 2 h; actometer activity unchanged.
DHEAS lower in CFS (sensitive and specific) while IGF1 and IGFBP3/IGF1 were normal.
GB virus-C seropositivity (2/12 vs 1/21) and active infection did not differ.
CFS-only patients had subtle deficits in processing speed, consistency and efficiency; 25 min light exercise neither worsened nor improved cognition.
note: Light exercise only; FM subgroup did not differ from controls

finding: Standard cut-offs on GHQ, HAM-D and HADS-D misclassified depression in CFS; 31% had depression on SCID.
Plasma isoprostanes and oxidised LDL were higher and HDL lower in CFS; isoprostanes correlated with symptoms including PEM in low-CV-risk patients.
Adolescents with CFS had greater functional impairment and favoured rest over exercise; psychiatric symptoms high in both groups.
Point prevalence of CFS 6.4% in a convenience survey; TCM syndrome typing described.
Urinary CFSUM1 and CFSUM2 reported earlier were derivatisation artefacts (pyroglutamic acid, serine), not CFS markers.
Patent for UHF radiation at acupuncture points.
Salivary cortisol and cortisone were lower across the day in CFS with preserved rhythm and unchanged cortisol/cortisone ratio.
Psychiatric disorders (32% current) did not alter outcome of CBT for CFS.
HLA-DQA1*01 was more frequent in CFS (51% vs 35%, OR 1.93, p=0.008).
Point prevalence of CFS 0.6% and chronic fatigue 8.4% in primary care.
PBMC microarray gave 35 differential genes, 16 confirmed by PCR (15 up, IL-10RA down), suggesting T-cell activation and mitochondrial/neuronal changes.
Total T, B, NK counts did not differ; CFS had more CD16+CD3- NK cells than MS.
Adolescents with CFS and their parents had lower internal health locus of control.
CDC Symptom Inventory had good reliability and separated CFS from controls and non-CFS fatigue.
No difference between CFS and CFS+FM in depression, attribution style or self-esteem.
Most physiological and cognitive measures were reliable across weeks; mental and physical fatigue ratings fluctuated.
note: Authors infer central basis of fatigue

finding: Free tryptophan and free Trp/CAA ratio were higher in CFS (+48%, +43%), suggesting a high-serotonin subgroup.
Hydrokinesotherapy associated with clinical improvement and a change in buccal cell nuclear Z-potential.
note: Russian-language, obscure endpoint, not clearly CFS

finding: Subsets of CFS had more antibodies to MAP2 (p=0.03) and ssDNA (p=0.04); no excess of common nuclear/cellular autoantibodies.
note: Sample size not in abstract, modest p values

finding: Analysis shows the recommended fatigue scales reach their extreme scores in many items, so poorly capture severe CFS fatigue.
24-h blood sampling showed reduced ACTH (esp 8-10 am) but no differences in cortisol, GH or prolactin or cortisol rhythm.
note: Small; cortisol not lower in serum

finding: fMRI during auditory working memory showed CFS patients recruit wider verbal working-memory networks for equal accuracy, interpreted as greater effort.
note: Small, labelled trial in source but is imaging

finding: 48% of GPs were not confident diagnosing CFS/ME and 41% not confident treating it.
CFS patients without psychiatric comorbidity showed no heart rate or galvanic skin response evidence of exercise phobia.
note: Argues against a phobia explanation of exercise avoidance

finding: Patent for carbinol compounds for fibromyalgia/CFS.
Joint mobility and collagen markers did not differ, but systolic blood pressure was 13.5 mmHg lower in adolescent CFS.

population: Fatigue syndromes in UK primary care
finding: Patients labelled ME had the longest illness (CFS/ME median 80 days/yr), PVFS the best prognosis.
Case series of CFS onset after occupational insecticide exposure; a third also had multiple chemical sensitivity.
Report summary advocating a biopsychosocial view and CBT.
After 70% max cycling, exercise-responsive PBMC gene expression differed between CFS and controls, with ion-transport and chromatin genes prominent.
CFS patients raised daily activity 28% for 4 weeks but muscle pain and mood worsened.
2-5A trimers/tetramers protect native RNase L from proteolysis; CFS extracts with 37-kDa RNase L preferentially make 2-5A dimers.
A 0-100% functional ability scale was rated workable by 99% of young people.
Low-dose synacthen test gave lower cortisol in adolescent CFS, more pronounced in females.
note: Pattern suggests reduced central drive rather than adrenal failure

finding: Descriptive Chinese case series: memory complaints in 84%, anti-BDV p24 and erythrocyte n-6 fatty acids and carnitine measured (results truncated).
Pooled placebo response across CFS trials was 19.6% (95% CI 15.4-23.7), varying by intervention type.
Stimulated PBMC TGF-beta1 mRNA and production were lower in CFS.
note: In vitro stimulated, small; opposite to reports of raised serum TGF-beta

finding: Peak VO2 was lower in CFS patients with deregulated RNase L than with normal RNase L, with no sex effect.
EBV dUTPase induced proinflammatory cytokines in PBMC and sickness behaviours (temperature rise, weight and activity loss) in mice.
No differences in basal cortisol, urinary free cortisol, DHEAS, IGF-1 or ACTH/cortisol responses to CRH or naloxone.
Severity ratings and standardised measures may improve CFS diagnostic criteria sensitivity and specificity.
Subjective quality of life was lower in CFS than in mental disorders; depressive symptoms best predicted it.
After a psychosocial stress test, LPS-stimulated IL-6 and TNF-alpha production fell in CFS but rose in controls.
Parents of children with CFS reported more CFS-like illness, distress and family burden than JRA parents.
Thesis literature review applying attachment theory to patient-professional relationships.
Thesis on an osteopathic CSF and lymphatic drainage treatment with symptom questionnaires, muscle function and MRI; results truncated.
Narrative review: CFS is rare relative to fatigue, and many clinic associations are absent in community samples.
Urinary electrophoretic (MEKC) peaks differed in CFS and CFS/FM versus controls, proposed as biomarkers.
note: Pilot, sample size not in abstract

finding: Patients had lower peak activity (8,654 vs 12,913, p=0.003) but similar average activity; activity related to pain.
Hypothesis review proposing nitric oxide-driven central sensitisation via RNase L/PKR/NF-kB for CFS pain.
Atopy history and prick tests did not differ between CFS and controls.
Non-standard claim that interstitial pneumonia equals CFS treated with vitamin C and DHEA-cortisol.
Hypothesis that ACTH autoantibodies disrupt the HPA axis in CFS, with corticosteroid replacement as treatment.
Delayed liquid (23/32) and solid (12/32) gastric emptying in CFS, correlating with GI symptom scores.
Patent for a Chinese herbal preparation for fatigue.
Cortisol was lower in CFS, with normal FSH, LH, estradiol and progesterone in both menstrual phases; depression did not alter hormones.
58% of CFS patients had previously undiagnosed primary sleep disorders (apnoea, periodic limb movements) on polysomnography; psychological maladjustment resembled narcolepsy.
CFS/ME diagnoses rose from 9% to 26% of fatigue diagnoses 1990-2001 while fatigue symptom reporting was flat; more common in females.
Only 16% of population CFS cases had been diagnosed; sudden onset and middle income predicted diagnosis.
Central activation failure during sustained maximal contraction was greater in CFS (36.5% vs 12.9%) with less peripheral fatigue.
Triple-blind randomised trial of homeopathy in CFS (no abstract in record).
note: No abstract available; judged by title only

finding: Peak VO2 can be predicted from peak workload on bicycle ergometry (r=0.89) in CDC-defined CFS.
Social support, not healthcare support, related to quality of life.
Differential-display PCR of PBMC in one case-control pair found 10 verified differentially expressed genes, mostly present at baseline.
Voxel-based morphometry showed reduced grey matter in bilateral prefrontal cortex in CFS, tracking fatigue severity.
Kinesiophobia scale (TSK-CFS) had good reliability and associated with disability measures.
CFS had lower daytime activity and less regular activity-rest cycles.
On submaximal cycling, activity-matched controls differed only in perceived effort (higher in CFS) and final power output.
note: Authors propose effort sense or avoidance

finding: During handgrip tasks CFS showed poorer motor performance and greater EEG theta power.
At 44 months 8% of fatigued employees were CFS-like cases; predictors included age, exhaustion, female sex, low education.
Patent for substance P antagonists.
Narrative review of MRS: early muscle acidosis on 31P-MRS in a subset and raised brain choline on 1H-MRS, with oxidative stress proposed.
Hochu-ekki-to increased running activity and lowered spleen IL-10 mRNA in a mouse CFS model.
Neutrophils from CFS patients showed more apoptosis, annexin V binding and TNF-R1 expression, with raised active TGF-beta1.
note: TGF-beta1 handling artefact possible per later work

finding: CFS twins reported more sleepiness (ESS 10.9 vs 8.2) but multiple sleep latency test did not differ from healthy co-twins.
Corticosteroid-binding globulin Ser224 homozygosity showed only a trend (p=0.07) in CFS; CBG levels differed by genotype.
73% had high fear of movement but kinesiophobia did not correlate with exercise capacity or disability.
fMRI of motor imagery showed slower responses in CFS and altered anterior cingulate activity during errors.
Rehabilitation programme with graded activities: 43% complete resolution versus 4.5% with supportive care alone.
Weighted prevalence of CFS-like illness in adolescents 338 per 100,000; none of 11 evaluated met CFS definition.

n: 15 CFS, 12 both, 13 FM vs matched controls
finding: 24-h ACTH and cortisol pulsatility showed no significant differences in CFS (cortisol numerically lower overnight); FM differed.
Basal DHEA was higher in CFS (14.1 vs 9.0 ng/ml) with DHEAS unchanged; also tested CRH response and 1 month hydrocortisone 5 or 10 mg versus placebo.
Abnormal cardiac wall motion in 11.5% at rest of CFS patients vs 2% of cancer controls, attributed to EBV/CMV cardiomyopathy.
note: Single group, non-matched controls, claim speculative

finding: Modelled productivity loss from CFS of about $9.1 billion per year in the US.
Patent for transdermal testosterone gel.
Time-frequency analysis of HRV/BPV during tilt showed a subtle autonomic difference even in CFS without POTS.
GPs negatively stereotyped CFS patients compared with IBS.
Patent for herbal medicine for female CFS.
Systematic review: most CFS patients unemployed; only depression linked to unemployment; CBT, rehabilitation and exercise therapy associated with return to work.
CFS patients reported more negative social interactions; these fell after CBT but not support groups.
CD4 and CD8 counts and CD56+ NK cells were lower in CFS, with higher CD4/CD8 ratio; NK counts higher in post-infectious than non-post-infectious CFS.
3.6% CFS-like caseness among employees at follow-up (incidence 85 per 10,000/yr); 0.36% physician-diagnosed.
81% had an abnormal sleep factor; CFS had markedly higher odds of non-restorative sleep (adjusted OR 28.1).
No cognitive difference between CFS and healthy co-twins, but both twin groups were slower than unrelated controls on speed-dependent tests.
ACTH response to insulin tolerance test was reduced in CFS and inversely related to illness duration (r=-0.59).
Morning cortisol was lower in CFS and FM than controls; other pituitary-gonadal hormones were largely normal.
CFS patients fell about 1 SD below controls on 9 of 18 tests, with deficits in attention, processing and motor speed but not memory or executive function.
At mean 4.6 years only 25% of CFS had near-complete improvement, 44% none; fatigue under 6 months all recovered.

population: Paediatric CFS vs JIA vs emotional disorders
finding: Children with CFS had greater functional impairment and school non-attendance than comparison groups.
IgM antibody to EBV VCA positive in 33 of 58 CFS, proposed as a marker for an EBV subset.
note: Single group; controls 9 years older; unconventional serology

finding: Exercise capacity (peak VO2 etc.) correlated moderately (rho about 0.3) with self-reported activity limitation.
No increase in sexual dysfunction in CFS.
Two-thirds of CFS patients reduced alcohol intake, mainly because of increased tiredness afterwards.
Short commentary arguing low-to-moderate intermittent exercise therapy helps CFS and that testing does not worsen symptoms.
note: Narrative, claim conflicts with later PEM evidence

finding: Personality disorder in 39% of CFS vs 73% depressed vs 4% healthy.
Salivary cortisol response to awakening (AUC) was lower in CFS.
Greater heart-rate rise and systolic BP fall on standing in CFS; erythropoietin and haematology normal.
note: Authors suggest deconditioning; EPO in reference range

finding: Polysomnography showed more stage 3 and REM sleep in CFS twins than co-twins, with no major sleep architecture abnormality; some respiratory impairment.
Pregnancy did not consistently worsen CFS (29% worse, 30% better); spontaneous abortions more frequent after onset (30% vs 8%).
After stimulation CD4/CD8 T cells showed a Th2/Tc2 bias with similar IFN-gamma, IL-2, IL-10; unstimulated cells had more IFN-gamma or IL-4 producers.
At 5 years severe work disability persisted and only 3% neared recovery (<6% substantially better).
Plasma progesterone metabolites were higher in CFS, notably isopregnanolone (2.3-fold, p<=0.001).
Kuibitang herbal inhibited LPS-induced TNF-alpha, IL-10 and TGF-beta1 in PBMC from CFS patients.

population: CFS vs Gulf War vs OP exposure
finding: Forearm skin blood flow response to iontophoresed acetylcholine was higher in CFS but normal in Gulf War and OP-exposed groups.
Educational graded-activity intervention benefits (55% no longer meeting criteria) maintained at 2 years.

population: CFS (CDC) sporadic vs Gulf War vs OP
finding: Groups meeting CDC-1994 criteria differed in symptom severity and function, suggesting heterogeneity.
Symptom factor and cluster analysis showed CFS overlaps substantially with non-CFS unexplained fatigue.
Staphylococcal toxoid vaccine induced antibody responses that paralleled clinical improvement.
Software for continuous baroreflex sensitivity and effectiveness analysis during 45-min tilt in five groups; no results in abstract.
Narrative review of occupational therapy for CFS.
Thesis: women with CFS/ME felt disbelieved and let down by services.
Tilt-derived hemodynamic instability and fractal scores distinguished CFS (HIS sens 84.5%, spec 85.1%); pilot midodrine corrected dysautonomia before fatigue improved.
note: Review with pilot data, single group

finding: Pilot of expressive writing in CFS assessed feasibility and experience.
Review of TCM understanding and treatment of CFS.
Diurnal activity time series showed more abrupt interruptions of activity in CFS by wavelet analysis; nocturnal activity did not differ.
Whole-body periodic acceleration (passive exercise device) reportedly eased FM and CFS symptoms; nitric oxide hypothesis.
note: Abstract gives no numbers or controls

finding: Case of CFS with positive ANA developing postpartum thyroiditis.
Hypothesis that RNase L/PKR dysregulation causes channelopathy, intracellular hypomagnesaemia and excess nitric oxide limiting exercise responses.
Hypothesis of autoimmunity to vasoactive neuropeptides (VIP, PACAP) after infection via molecular mimicry.
Therapists adhered to CBT manual in 87% of sessions and found CFS harder to treat than other conditions.
Yixinle oral liquid modified catecholamine and adrenal ascorbic acid changes in a mouse fatigue model.

population: CFS with and without psychiatric history, RA, healthy
finding: CFS without psychiatric history had slowed information processing but intact working memory; CFS with psychiatric comorbidity did not differ.
Consumer-driven rehabilitation programme improved symptom severity (d=0.71) and quality of life (d=0.66) versus delayed control.
Yeast-based dietary supplement reportedly improved clinical status in CFS with obesity.
CFS subjects used more drugs overall, particularly analgesics, hormones, antidepressants and benzodiazepines.
Red cell membrane arachidonic acid and DHA were lower, palmitic and oleic acid higher in CFS.
Blood gene expression distinguished subgroups only when stratified by illness onset, implicating purine/pyrimidine metabolism, glycolysis and oxidative phosphorylation genes.
Plasma cysteine/sulphate ratio was abnormal in 80 of 81 chronically ill nutrition-clinic patients (ME among several diagnoses) versus 2 of 177 controls.
note: Nutrition clinic, non-standard, ME not defined

finding: Anti-BDV p24 antibody positive in 11.5% of CFS vs 0% of controls (p<0.01).
Patent claiming Mycoplasma detection in blood cells as indicator of CFS.
Narrative guide to patient-centred management of CFS in primary care.
Longer serotonin transporter promoter alleles were more frequent in CFS (p<0.05).

population: Mixed chronic disease (ME one of several)
finding: Self-management course gave small improvements in a mixed disease group.
HADS fitted a three-factor better than two-factor structure in CFS.
Bojungikki-tang herbal inhibited LPS-induced TNF-alpha, IL-6, IL-10 and TGF-beta1 (about 48-64%) in CFS PBMC.
CFS identified in 50% of 86 patients with prior borreliosis or tick-borne encephalitis (71% after borreliosis).
Hyperaemic flow and PCr recovery were normal at baseline; partial cuff restriction reduced flow and slowed oxygen saturation recovery in CFS, but muscle metabolism did not differ.
note: 31P-MRS, Doppler and NIRS; refutes muscle oxidative defect

finding: Over 3 years only 20-33% still met CFS; 57% ever had partial/total remission, 10% sustained remission; shorter duration predicted remission.
Functional status in CFS did not differ from non-CFS medically or psychiatrically explained fatigue.
Reported altered isoprenoid pathway metabolites (low Na-K ATPase, ubiquinone, glutathione; high lipid peroxidation, nitric oxide) in CFS.
note: Speculative, non-standard metabolite claims, controls not stated

finding: Survey in a GP clinic: 29/36 recovered or much improved; education impact significant.
CFS patients held more negative illness perceptions than RA patients, with similar physical disability.
Sociological analysis of selfhood under a contested diagnosis.
Differential display found 12 expressed sequences upregulated in CFS lymphocytes including cathepsin C and MAIL1.
Severe life events or difficulties in the 3 months before onset were far more common in CFS (OR 9).
2-5A synthetase activity detected in 86% and 32% of CFS (two hospitals) vs 11% of controls; EBV EA-IgG and Coxiella serology in minorities.
CFS patients showed a significant first-night effect on polysomnography across several sleep parameters.
Baroreflex sensitivity fell more on standing in CFS, significantly only in severe CFS; BP maintained on standing.
Peak VO2 did not differ between Gulf War veterans with CFS (28.9 vs 30.8 mL/kg/min, p=0.39) and controls.
note: Gulf War population, single maximal test

finding: Skin acetylcholine-induced vasodilatation was prolonged in CFS (decay to 50% 24.5 vs 15.1 min, p=0.03), peak unchanged.
Recovery at one year associated with lower life stress.
Review plus study of low-dose (1 ug) ACTH test in CFS; prior literature on HPA function inconsistent (abstract truncated before results).
After 20 min cycling at 70% max, complement C4a (not C3a/C5a) rose at 6 h only in CFS.
Cortisol response to stress test was normal but in vitro dexamethasone inhibition of LPS-stimulated IL-6 and TNF-alpha was greater in CFS (enhanced glucocorticoid sensitivity).
Systematic review: low NK cell findings were inversely related to study quality; no consistent pattern of immune abnormality.
Peak VO2 lower and perceived exertion higher in CFS; free tryptophan higher and tyrosine lower during exercise, suggesting central serotonergic/dopaminergic changes.
Anti-muscarinic M1 receptor antibodies found in 53% of CFS (p<0.0001 vs controls); linked to muscle weakness score.
Stroke volume and cardiac output were lower in severe CFS than in controls and milder CFS.
Sarcoplasmic reticulum membranes from CFS muscle showed altered Na/K and Ca ATPase and ryanodine channel behaviour with higher membrane fluidity.
CFS patients more often had acute infectious onset (80% vs 43%) and less psychiatric comorbidity than chronic fatigue without CFS.
Hypothesis that atypical depression in CFS is sickness behaviour.
Point prevalence 235 per 100,000 (373 women, 83 men), incidence about 180 per 100,000/yr.
FDG-PET: 14 of 26 had hypometabolism, mostly in cingulate and mesial cortex; reductions correlated with anxiety/depression, not fatigue.
Tertiary-care CFS had more frequent symptoms than community CFS.
Opinion essay on fatigue and clinical examination in CFS.
No difference in post-ischaemic or post-exercise hyperaemic flow, PCr recovery or oxygen resaturation.
Serum protein carbonyls were higher in CFS (p<0.0005).
Narrative argument that lactic acid bacteria may help CFS.
44% of fatigued sick-leave employees met CFS research criteria and resembled diagnosed CFS patients.

population: CFS vs chronic fatigue in UK primary care (CDC)
finding: Only 31% of GP fatigue patients met CDC CFS criteria; CFS group had worse function and distress and more unemployment.
Same isoprenoid-pathway biochemical profile claims (low Na-K ATPase, ubiquinone, glutathione; high digoxin, lipid peroxidation).
note: Duplicate/related to 26983655; speculative, controls not described

finding: Maternal overprotection and depression associated with CFS diagnosis; childhood illness similar.
CD56+CD3+CD8+ cell numbers were higher in CFS than metropolitan controls; cluster vs non-cluster area controls differed.
Psychiatric illness or personality disorder did not explain physical impairment in CFS.
Changes in reaction and movement time tracked changes in corticospinal excitability on TMS across two visits.
CFS twins reported worse sleep and had more REM sleep than healthy co-twins, with little other objective difference.
CFS-APQ questionnaire showed adequate validity and reliability.
Concurrent psychiatric illness did not worsen physical functioning in CFS but reduced emotional well-being.
CFS patients made more somatic interpretations of ambiguous words and were slower on Stroop, without attentional bias.
Philosophical critique of non-falsifiable hypotheses in CFS research.
Mycoplasma 52%, C. pneumoniae 7.5% and active HHV-6 30.5% in CFS blood versus 6%, 1% and 9% in controls.
note: PCR from one group; not replicated in controlled studies

finding: CFS had higher illness worry than MS; somatic attributions and neuroticism predicted worry in both.
Peak VO2 and RPE relative to peak did not differ; RPE higher only at absolute workloads; controls exercised longer.
RPE higher at every workload in Gulf War CFS, but self-reported fatigue explained the difference; peak variables similar.
Bronchial hyperresponsiveness in 53% of CFS; BHR+ patients showed more T-cell phenotype differences; no link with RNase L cleavage.
Disability consequences were greatest in FM and CFS groups at a specialty clinic.
Patent for heterocyclic amine/cabergoline compounds.
58% attributed CFS to physical causes; attributions related to general attributional style.
Vascular (70%) and dystrophic (53%) eye pathology reported in CFS, exceeding controls.
No difference in cortisol response to low- or high-dose ACTH; primary adrenal insufficiency unlikely.
RNase L 37/83 kDa ratio above 0.4 gave 91% sensitivity and 71% specificity for CFS.
Patent for cholestyramine and alpha-MSH.
Patent for cytokine-ratio diagnostic test in lymphocytes.
1H-MRS of left basal ganglia showed raised choline compounds in CFS (p<0.001).
Psychiatric disorder in prior year in 72% of CFS vs 34% JIA, with more personality problems.
Mean 3-month cost about 1906 GBP, over 90% from informal care and lost work; CFS higher than non-CFS fatigue.
Tilt-derived haemodynamic instability score above -0.98 identified CFS with overall specificity 84.5%; 22% could not complete tilt.
Fractal HRV component fell more with tilt in CFS (cutoff gave 90% sensitivity, 72% specificity).
Essay comparing neglect of CFS/ME with HIV research.
Thesis summarising basal ganglia 1H-MRS abnormalities and impaired cardiovascular responses to exercise in a CFS subset.
Hypothesis that CFS may be a risk factor for osteopenia.
